human_tolerance.notes: Common in gardens, parks, shrublands and woodland edges; readily uses suburban feeders and dense shrubs or low trees for nesting. Tolerance values are authored for the simulation from that qualitative habitat association.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Males defend territories with song; exact simulation window is placed around the nesting season.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Two to four clutches can be produced each year; the longer southern garden window is a judgement around the described repeated broods.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Outside peak breeding, cardinals remain resident and may travel in mated pairs or small loose groups around feeders and cover.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Judgement: the female builds a cup nest of twigs, bark strips and grasses in dense shrub or a low tree 1-3 m off the ground, and the species raises two to four clutches of three or four eggs a year; the article does not date the nesting season.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Territory-holding males sing through the spring and summer; two to four clutches of three to four eggs are laid between March and August, with 12-13 days of incubation.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Males hold territory by song; two to four clutches a year.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: The female builds a well-concealed cup nest 1-3 m up in dense shrub or a low tree and incubates 12-13 days; young fledge 10-11 days after hatching.

vocalizations.description: Clear repeated whistled phrases such as 'cheer, cheer, cheer' and 'what-cheer, what-cheer', sung by both sexes from perches.
Short metallic chip call given when predators approach the nest or cover.
Brief chip notes used by paired birds and birds moving through shrubs or feeder edges.
Soft close-range notes associated here with beak-to-beak courtship feeding and pair contact.
A short, sharp, metallic chip, given as a contact or alarm note.

taxonomy.note: Linnaeus 1758, Cardinalis cardinalis; family Cardinalidae per the GBIF backbone and ITIS TSN 179124.

external.note: GBIF usage key and iNaturalist taxon id were also confirmed directly against their APIs; Wikidata provides NCBI taxon id (P685), ITIS TSN (P815), eBird code (P3444), and iNaturalist id (P3151). Wikidata licence verified from Wikidata:Licensing.

common_names.note: Labels and sitelinks for English, French, German and Dutch common names.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 and the Wikipedia infobox both report least concern.

range.note: Country list derived from the distribution text: southeastern Canada, eastern and southern United States, Mexico, northern Guatemala and Belize. Bermuda is listed as introduced. Cfa is included for the Shreveport/Louisiana locale; other climate classes across the broad range are intentionally omitted rather than over-enumerated.

traits.limb_count.note: Biped: two legs; the wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Wikipedia describes it as a ground feeder that finds food while hopping through trees or shrubbery; flight is implicit in the described bird body and territorial behaviour from tree tops.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Winter heat-retention behaviour and shivering are described for this bird.

traits.skin.note: Feathers: plumage described in detail in the Description section.

traits.flight.note: Powered flight between perches, trees and feeders.

traits.respiration.note: Authored from avian body plan; no separate respiratory source was needed beyond the source establishing the species as a bird.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Authored from the described bird life cycle of egg, nestling, juvenile and adult; no metamorphic larval stage is described.

traits.nest_type.note: Female builds a cup nest of twigs, bark strips, grasses and fibers.

traits.perching.note: Mid-sized perching songbird; males sing from tree tops or high locations.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg below 0.05 kg. EltonTraits licence verified from figshare API metadata.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BirdFuncDat BodyMass-Value 42.64 g converted to kilograms.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives adult annual survival of 60-65%, but no typical lifespan. A rough constant-hazard estimate using midpoint survival 0.625 gives 1/(1-0.625)=2.67 adult years; rounded down to 2.5 y to avoid false precision.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits lists Diet-PlantO 70, Diet-Fruit 10, Diet-Inv 20. Wikipedia says adults eat mainly weed seeds, grains and fruits, up to 90%, and also insects; PlantO is mapped to schema seed because the text explicitly identifies seeds/grains as the main plant food.

traits.social.note: Mated pairs often travel together, can stay together year-round, and flocking outside breeding is represented by allowing small groups at feeders; group_size maximum is authored judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal=0; Wikipedia describes song, feeding and territorial behaviour during dawn/day/dusk rather than night.

traits.defense.note: Authored mapping: alarm-chip near predators, then flee to dense shrubs or perches.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: common in gardens and at feeders but still a wild songbird that flees when closely approached.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits foraging strata: ground 40, understory 20, mid-high 20, canopy 20. Understory/mid-high/canopy are mapped to arboreal for the schema.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Habitat includes shrublands and gardens; nests are well concealed in dense shrub or low tree.

habitat.resources.note: Food tags reflect EltonTraits diet and Wikipedia's seeds/grains/fruits/insects, including young fed almost entirely insects. Perch, shrub_thicket and nest_cup reflect perching song and dense-shrub cup nesting.

habitat.requires.note: Judgement from nesting in well-concealed dense shrubs or low trees; 40 m is an authored placement radius for the simulation.

habitat.suitability.note: Judgement curves for a suburban garden species associated with gardens, shrublands, woodland edges and dense cover interspersed with open areas.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: uses_gardens and Adapter affinity from garden, park and feeding-station descriptions; numeric tolerance settings are authored judgement for the simulation.

seasonal.strategy.note: Distribution map and text describe the species as year-round across its range, and pairs may stay together year-round.

seasonal.phases.note: Territory, breeding, multiple broods and pair behaviour are sourced; exact calendar boundaries are judgement for a southern US garden.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Incubation takes 12 or 13 days; young fledge 10 or 11 days after hatching; juvenile beak and plumage change by fall. Juvenile duration and scale are authored approximations for preview/import.

activity.note: Placeholder before running tools/fetch_activity.py; replaced by US-LA activity provenance after the fetch.

vocalizations.song.note: Clear whistled patterns repeated and then varied, both sexes singing and the male singing from a high perch to defend territory; the recorded phrases include 'what-cheer, what-cheer', 'purty, purty, purty' and 'cheer, cheer, cheer, what'. Sung year-round.

vocalizations.alarm.note: Short metallic chip when predators approach the nest.

vocalizations.contact_chip.note: Authored from the same chip-call description and mated-pair movement; Wikipedia does not separately quantify a contact call.

vocalizations.courtship_feed.note: Authored quiet pair-contact call around courtship feeding; the beak-to-beak courtship feeding behaviour is sourced but a specific quiet note is not quantified.

look.note: Male look uses brilliant crimson plumage, black face mask, coral beak, darker back/wings, strong cone-shaped beak and prominent raised crest from Wikipedia; proportions, colours and extra-part dimensions are judgement for a readable block model.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for bt-perching-songbird-v1. food_tag=seed matches the main adult diet and habitat resource; nest window March-August reflects repeated broods; flee and cooldown values are judgement for a garden songbird.

vocalizations.chip.note: Wikipedia describes a distinctive short metallic chip as the alarm call; the cooldown is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: Song and alarm descriptions from Wikipedia's vocalisation section (clear repeated whistled patterns sung by both sexes, songs learned and regionally variable; short metallic chip at the nest). Time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement since no open source quantifies them.
